chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: Atlantic Records starts: Old Black Magic and Rock the House
summary: He describes Atlantic's origin with Ahmet Ertegun and Herb Abramson in a hotel room and recording in Cleveland.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I had a five-piece band. But when that engagement broke up they all left except myself and Ted Prysock. And we just hung in town, and first thing you know we got this job for a couple of weeks. That's why I say we sent for Jerry Potter. He lives right up the block from me. Very good drummer, man, excellent. And he came out and then we got a piano player and a bass out there and at that time I had made some records for Atlantic. See it helped start Atlantic Records off, in a room no larger than this -- little hotel room. Ahmet Ertegun, Herb Abrams, he had a little studio called A-1 studio. And the three of us sittin' there, and that's where Atlantic Records got started. And then they proceeded to step on everybody's nose from then on to get a step higher -- they didn't care about you after -- 'cause I made some good records there, man.
How did you get to make the records? Did they see you perform.

Yeah. Probably 52nd Street I guess, I don't know, just word-of-mouth. He came in town because Herb was with National Records and he got him because he knew -- Herb Abrams knows recording backwards. So the other fella had the money. But anyhow we got this date started
and I did the date and forgot all about it -- was called "Old Black Magic" I think was one of the records. ---

B. Atlantic records came all the way out to Cleveland to record me. Yeah they made a trip out there, while I was at this place. And I made a number called "Rock the House" and it was a hit, along with "Annie Laurie" I think was one of em -- "Frankie and Johnny" probably, and a slow blues "Blue Harlem" again -- I must have made that eight times.
